name: Pine Cliffs Hotel
positioning: Pine Cliffs Hotel, a Luxury Collection Resort, Algarve: a traditionally styled, Moorish-influenced hotel at the heart of Pine Cliffs Resort, on top of the Falésia cliffs above the Atlantic
best_for: Couples and families wanting a clifftop resort a short walk from the beach
Golfers wanting a 9-hole clifftop course on site
Families wanting a kids' club and tennis academy on the grounds

facts.text: The resort sits at the top of the cliffs of Falésia on the Algarve coast, with views over the Atlantic Ocean.
Pine Cliffs Hotel is at the heart of Pine Cliffs Resort, a five-minute walk from the beach.
The hotel's architecture is inspired by the region's heritage and has Moorish influences.
Bed headboards, bathrooms, internal courtyards and fountains are decorated with local Portuguese tiles in a blue, white and yellow color scheme.
Rooms and suites look out over the Albufeira coast, the Atlantic Ocean or the gardens.
The Pine Cliffs Golf Course is a 9-hole course designed by Martin Hawtree, perched above the Atlantic.
The Serenity Spa's thermal oasis includes an indoor hydro pool, herbal sauna, salt sauna, ice fountain and experience showers.
Outdoor pools are set among the hotel gardens, and the main pool has cliff-top views along the coast.
The Annabel Croft Tennis Academy has floodlit clay and all-weather hard courts on the hotel grounds.
The Porto Pirata kids' club has life-size pirate ships, a children's pool and an 18-hole mini-golf course.
Maré is a beach restaurant steps from the ocean, serving freshly caught fish and seafood.

highlights.text: The resort sits on top of the Falésia cliffs on the Algarve coast, looking out over the Atlantic Ocean.
The hotel is traditionally styled, with Portuguese history told through murals and hand-painted tiles.
The golf course's signature Par 3 sixth hole, the Devil's Parlour, calls for a carrying shot over the cliffs above a ravine.
The Serenity Spa's signature treatment uses Algarve ingredients such as fleur-de-sel from Ria Formosa, sand from Falésia Beach, carob and orange oil.
Mirador Champagne Bar sits at the very edge of the cliffs, serving champagne and cocktails.

considerations.text: The resort is large, and Condé Nast Traveler says its size can take some getting used to.
Restaurants and bars are subject to seasonal opening.
Access to the spa's thermal oasis is not complimentary.
